messages:
maria: Quick smoke from onboarding the new panoptic-7B fork — saw a weird pattern when we run longcontext evals across Llama/Mistral/Gemma/Qwen variants. Posting short logs and a couple questions.

ajay: dropping the high-level: int4 quant on panoptic gives ~1.8x perf but on Gemma-derived weights we see 6-8% token-wise quality delta vs fp16 on long (2k+) sequences.

maria: repro steps I used: `./eval_runner --model panoptic7b-int4 --dataset long-context-2000 --seed 42 --batch 8`

maria: metrics snapshot: `perplexity: fp16=12.3, int4=13.1, rougeL: fp16=0.42, int4=0.39`

teo: did you compare rotary params? Gemma->Qwen conversions sometimes need headwise phase scaling. If headmap mismatch, KV cache lookup can misalign and cause token drift.

maria: Yep. I tried both `rotary_scale=1.0` and `rotary_scale=0.707` in the conversion. The weirdness reduces with headwise scaling but doesn't vanish.

eva: Any vocab mapping issues? If token ids are remapped (surface-level aliasing) the early tokens will be fine but long-range prefix matching can break.

maria: Good call — I dumped token ids for a failing sample and saw a run where pad token swapped from 50256 -> 0 after converter. That's probably from our quickmap script.

samir: That pad swap will absolutely shift KV indices once cached. Even an off-by-one for BOS/EOS causes phase mismatch over many heads.

maria: I ran a cross-check: convert with strict-vocab=true (reject remaps) vs permissive. Strict-vocab avoids the pad swap and improves int4 rougeL by ~1.5 pts, but latency/size same.

ajay: Interesting. So two orthogonal issues: rotary/headwise scaling + vocab remapping. Which is the dominant regression?

maria: For our sample set, vocab remap explains ~60% of regressions; rotary mismatch explains the rest. However, on Mistral-derived models rotary scaling explains more (closer to 70%).

teo: On the kernel side, make sure per-head cosine/sin indexing aligns. We had a previous bug where `head_dim % 64` packing changed layout for Gemma-converted tensors. Might interact badly with int4 packing.

maria: Good note. I saw some odd memcpy patterns in the int4 runtime when head_dim=128 vs 80. I'll instrument the packing code to assert expected strides.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist update: added `convert.strict_vocab` flag and `rotary.scale_candidate` matrix to onboarding CI for panoptic-7B.

eva: For the eval harness, can you add a small regression test that forces pad/token id aliasing? We should catch this earlier.

maria: Will add tests: (1) strict-vocab roundtrip, (2) headwise-rotary-scale sweep 0.5/0.707/1.0, (3) int4 vs fp16 sample diffs > 3% rouge.

samir: Also log KV-cache hashes per request id so we can bisect where phase drift starts. That helped us isolate similar issue on orion-rt.

maria: Plan: patch converter to fail on pad remap, add head-dim stride asserts, run CI sweep overnight, and report a short benchmark in morning.

teo: If you hit a kernel packing bug, ping infra — we may need a microkernel change rather than a conversion-only fix.

maria: Thanks all — pushing a tiny PR now: https://git.redwood/panoptic/convert/pull/487 :eyes:

ajay: Nice. Leave one sample trace pinned here once CI finishes so we can compare the token-level diffs. :thumbsup:
